body:
## What happened

On PR #2216, CodeRabbit's first review (2026-11-10T10:32:20Z) flagged `features/step_definitions/support/per-agent-mlflow-helpers.ts` (lines ~39-41 and 231): a 'late-ending child span' test scenario ended a span after a fixed `setTimeout(..., 75ms)` while `runLateSpanDispatcherRequest` separately waited a fixed `setTimeout(resolve, 100ms)` — two independent fixed delays racing each other with no synchronization, a genuine CI-flakiness risk on a slow runner. The fullsend-ai-review bot's two review rounds (11:03 and 14:41 UTC, 10 inline findings total) never touched this file or mentioned timing/race/flakiness anywhere; its findings covered production-code logic, data-exposure, naming, and documentation/ADR-scope issues only. The author fixed exactly the issue CodeRabbit raised, in commit c31ed870, replacing the fixed-delay wait with an awaited callback (`onLateChildEnded`/`perAgentLateChildEnded`) — confirming the risk was real and the fix matched CodeRabbit's suggestion closely.

## What could go better

The review agent's evaluation dimensions evidently don't include timing-determinism checks on test/step-definition code, even though this repo's own AGENTS.md has an extensive 'Keeping test output clean' section built around test-hygiene investigation (including a named 'Pattern: injectable error loggers' convention) — this repo has a demonstrated history of exactly this class of test-fixture bug. A generic external tool (CodeRabbit) caught this; the repo-aware, checklist-driven in-house review agent did not. Confidence is high that this specific miss is real (confirmed by reading the code and the later matching fix); confidence is moderate on how systemic the broader category gap is, since this is one data point from one repo.

## Proposed change

Add a review-agent check (in a correctness or test-quality evaluation dimension in fullsend-ai/agents, e.g. `review.md` or the relevant sub-agent skill) for new or changed test step-helpers/fixtures that use a fixed `setTimeout`/`sleep` delay to coordinate with asynchronous production code under test: flag it as a flakiness risk and recommend an awaited, deterministic signal (callback, promise, or event) instead of a fixed delay — mirroring the pattern CodeRabbit already applies generically.

## Validation criteria

On the next 10 PRs across repos using fullsend review that introduce or modify test helpers with fixed-delay waits coordinating with async code, the review agent should flag the pattern itself, without needing an external tool or human reviewer to catch it first. Track whether CodeRabbit or human reviewers continue to catch this class of issue that fullsend review misses.

## Related issues checked

Searched: review agent flaky setTimeout repo:redhat-et/hermes; test timing determinism review repo:redhat-et/hermes repo:fullsend-ai/agents repo:fullsend-ai/fullsend; coderabbit caught fullsend-ai-review missed repo:redhat-et/hermes repo:fullsend-ai/agents repo:fullsend-ai/fullsend; race condition span test flaky repo:redhat-et/hermes; staggered-arrival timing concurrency repo:fullsend-ai/agents
Considered: fullsend-ai/agents#714, fullsend-ai/fullsend#1444
#714 covers a staggered-arrival TOCTOU race in production Go concurrency code (singleflight/sync.Map), a different failure class from test-fixture flakiness. #1444 covers a one-off normalization-consistency bug on a different repo/PR (UI state misalignment caused by using raw vs. normalized state), unrelated to test timing. Neither covers detection of fixed-delay test-fixture flakiness.

---
_Generated by retro agent from https://github.com/redhat-et/hermes/pull/2216_
title: Review agent should flag fixed-delay (setTimeout/sleep) synchronization against async code in new test helpers as a flakiness risk

### Summary

As @rahulnakmol, I want the tests of `internal/cli` to run well below go test's 10-minute default, so that a PR build does not wait on one slow package and the 30-minute timeout of #1151 is a margin, not a need.

The package keeps getting slower:

| Where | Commit | `internal/cli` time |
|---|---|---|
| CI `build`, dev | bdd02c1 (run 40710734386) | 576 s |
| This orb's local gate (2 cores) | 4957f37 + #1123, 2026-10-27 | 787 s |
| This orb's local gate (2 cores) | 80af4e1, 2026-10-28 | 1008 s |

### Completion Goal

1. [metric] state: the CI `build` job of dev after the change, on ubuntu-latest; expected: `go test` reports `internal/cli` at 300 s or less
2. [metric] state: `bash .agents/check --full` on a 2-core orb after the change; expected: `internal/cli` takes 450 s or less
3. [api-trace] state: the test names of `internal/cli` before and after the change; expected: each test that ran before still runs, in `internal/cli` or in the package it moved to, so no coverage is lost

### Measure

Seconds that go test reports for `internal/cli` in the CI `build` job of dev, per run.

### Threshold

300 s or less on CI

### Scenario

A person pushes a PR. Its `build` job finishes `internal/cli` in under 5 minutes, and the local gate on a 2-core orb finishes it in under 8 minutes.

### Environment

go test of the module in CI (ubuntu-latest) and in a 2-core orb; never production

### Technical Owner

devops-devex-tinkerer

### Open questions

- deferred: Which costs most: tests that start git subprocesses, the device-flow fakes, or the mission world tests (`newMissionWorld`)? A profile of the slowest tests (`go test -json`, sorted by Elapsed) answers it before the plan. (It can wait: the plan profiles first, and #1151's timeout stops the failures now.)
- deferred: Split the package, run more tests in parallel, or share fixtures? (It can wait: the plan chooses after the profile.)
- deferred: Are 300 s on CI and 450 s on a 2-core orb the right thresholds? (It can wait: a person confirms them before Ready.)

### Checkpoints

1. A profile lists the slowest tests of `internal/cli` with their seconds (criteria 1, 2)
2. The CI `build` job of dev shows `internal/cli` at 300 s or less, with every earlier test still run (criteria 1, 3)
3. The local gate on a 2-core orb shows `internal/cli` at 450 s or less (criteria 2)

### Assumptions

#### Notes

#1151 gave the CI `build` and `integration` jobs `-timeout 30m`, and #1123 gave the local gate the same. Those stop random failures. They do not make the package faster.

#### Review guidance

- Check: no test is deleted to save time; criterion 3.
- Ignore: the time of other packages.
- Risk: more parallel tests can make shared fixtures flaky.

#### Behaviours

1. says: internal/cli's tests finish well below go test's 10-minute default; rule: always; source: criteria 1, 2

### Provenance

Request: "Also file the Story for internal/cli test speed under #889 (1008 s locally at 80af4e1, 787 s the day before, 576 s on CI) with grill, as status:planned, not Ready."
1. default (threshold): "internal/cli test speed"
2. default (threshold): "1008 s locally at 80af4e1"
3. default (scope): "internal/cli test speed"
title: internal/cli's tests run well below go test's 10-minute default

## Priority

P0, as requested by the owner for issues discovered during post-merge verification. Main CI is red; do not treat this revision as fully release-verified.

## Observed failure

Merged PR #63 at `68bd105a9d729c3af06d42188a87e7bba784fcb9`. The macOS push check failed:

- Run: https://github.com/itomek/lemonvox/actions/runs/42513887186
- Job: https://github.com/itomek/lemonvox/actions/runs/42513887186/job/128832568374
- Step: `Build, test and package without release credentials`
- `main/recorder_test.swift:25: Fatal error: Canceled permission unexpectedly recorded`
- `scripts/build.sh: line 46 ... Trace/BPT trap: 5 ... recorder-test`
- Exit code 133.

Runner: macOS 26.7.2 (25G332), macos-26-arm64 image 20261102.0473.1, Xcode 26.6, Swift 6.3.3.

The pre-merge PR macOS check passed on the same source tree: https://github.com/itomek/lemonvox/actions/runs/42513679351 . The post-merge Windows check and all 24 local Windows Release tests passed.

## Investigation context

`tests/recorder_test.swift` uses `FakePermission(.notDetermined)`, delays its grant by 50 ms, starts `Recorder.start()` in a Task, sleeps 10 ms, then cancels that Task. The failure is the assertion reached when `start.value` returns rather than throwing CancellationError. The test's timing dependency may matter under runner load, but root cause is not established. `Recorder.start()` already checks cancellation after awaiting permission; this result alone does not establish a production permission bypass. Permission is faked in this test, while the recorder implementation still uses AVAudioRecorder.

## Acceptance

- Reproduce and distinguish test scheduling/fixture flakiness from a production cancellation defect.
- Make the permission/cancellation ordering deterministic, avoiding dependence on two wall-clock sleeps.
- Preserve denied-permission behavior and cancellation after a late permission result; avoid recording real input while testing failure/cancellation paths.
- Add regression coverage for the established cause and obtain green macOS main checks, including packaging and downstream smoke tests.
title: [P0] macOS main CI fails recorder cancellation check after merge

body:
Found while running the `build` area for [#579](https://github.com/SuperQuentin/UnitSportSwitzerland/issues/579). Both reproduce on a clean `main` (3499d55a), so neither is caused by that work. Related: #376 already mentions "flaky checks" among the water follow-ups.

## 1. `--buildcheck` fails under `tools/test.sh`, passes standalone

```
[buildcheck] FAIL the grown wall broke on the 5th hit (1)
[buildcheck] FAIL a shot at the door wall chipped it (True)
[buildcheck] RESULT: FAILED (2)
```

- `GODOT=... tools/test.sh quick build` on a clean `main`: **FAIL**, reproducibly.
- `godot --headless --fixed-fps 60 --path . -- --buildcheck --systems ui,physics,build` by hand: **ok**, reproducibly.

So it is not `--fixed-fps` on its own — the runner adds something else (`guard_run`, the `user://` redirection, or the checks that ran before it in the same tier). The wall reads as ungrown at the moment of the first hit: metal is 500 HP once grown and a hit is 120, so breaking on hit 1 means its HP was under 120, i.e. `GrownHp` saw an age near 0 despite the probe's `await Seconds(Spec(Metal).Seconds + 0.3)`.

Worth knowing because the path-to-check map only selects `--buildcheck` for changes under `src/Build/`, so it is invisible unless you happen to touch that area.

## 2. `--swimcheck`'s "gamey" swell assertion is flaky

```
[swimcheck] FAIL gamey: the swell lifts and drops the swimmer 0.23 m
```

Three consecutive runs on clean `main`: 0.14 m **FAIL**, 0.18 m **FAIL**, 0.42 m **ok**. The measured heave varies by 3x run to run and the threshold sits inside that spread, so the check passes roughly one run in three. Same spread on a feature branch (0.12 / 0.15 / 0.23 / 0.32).

Either the probe needs to sample long enough for the spectrum to deliver a full swell, or the assertion needs to be about the mean rather than the extreme it currently catches.

## Why it matters

A tier that is red on `main` cannot tell anyone whether their own change broke something; both of these cost real time to rule out. Fixing or quarantining them (`@realtime`, a wider window, or a longer sample) would make the `build` and water areas trustworthy again.
title: Two quick-tier checks are red on main: --buildcheck under the runner, --swimcheck's gamey swell is flaky

## Story Statement

**As a** Pair maintainer
**I want** re-reviews that block only on the delta, and at most 3 fix groups per round with independent ones prepared in parallel
**So that** a card converges in at most 3 rounds instead of 4–6, and a 7-group round stops running serially (#641 Diagnosis, root causes 3 and 4).

**Where**: review-phase skill, `cycle-state.mjs` resolve, red-spec planner, `pair run` driver.

## Epic Context

**Parent Epic**: #605 · **Umbrella**: #641 (split 2026-11-14, slice 5 of 6; order #645 → #646 → #647 → #648 → #649 → #650)
**Status**: Refined
**Priority**: P0 (inherited from #641)

## Classification

`risk:red` · `cost:green`

<details>
<summary>Matrix: refinement</summary>

| Dimension | Tier | Source | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Criticality | green | `risk-matrix.md` | Low |
| Change/diff | red | scope | review blocking rules, planner, driver concurrency |
| Business | red | subdomain | Collaborative Workflow (Core): what blocks a merge |
| Security | yellow | paths | Critical/security findings always block |
| Coupling | yellow | map-contexts | driver concurrency ↔ cycle worktrees |

Confidence: high (carried from #641's matrix, scoped to this slice).

</details>

## Acceptance Criteria

Carried verbatim from #641 (ids kept).

### Functional Requirements

- **AC-14** **Given** a re-review, **when** it finds a new finding outside the delta, **then** that finding blocks only if Critical or security; otherwise a follow-up card is filed. Minor-only findings never open a round. After round 3, Minor-only goes to ready-for-merge with a follow-up, and an open Major escalates.
- **AC-16** **Given** a remediation round, **when** it is planned, **then** it has at most 3 groups. Groups with disjoint fixScope and no `dependsOn` are prepared and validated in parallel, and one verify runs on the merged head.

- **AC-D** **Given** this story changes the delivery process, a profile or a run setting, **when** it is done, **then** the docs describe the new behavior: the KB how-to and guidelines, the affected skill docs, the adoption `way-of-working.md`, the CLI help and README, with dataset and mirrors regenerated, and no doc still states the old behavior.

### Business Rules

- Critical and security findings always block; a deferred finding always gets a follow-up card.

### Edge Cases and Error Handling

- **Parallel groups touching the same path**: they run serially (the disjoint check fails closed).
- **Major still open after round 3**: escalate, never ready-for-merge.

## Test plan

| Behavior | AC | Level | Equivalence classes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| round rules | AC-14 | unit (`resolve`) | Minor-only, Major after r3, out-of-delta Critical |
| group cap and parallel | AC-16 | unit | disjoint, overlapping, `dependsOn` |

## Definition of Done Checklist

- [ ] AC-14, AC-16 met through public boundaries; failing behavior tests precede implementation
- [ ] Docs updated for the changed process, profile or setting (AC-D); dataset and mirrors regenerated
- [ ] Existing custody and contract tests green; dataset and mirrors regenerated where skills change
- [ ] Decisions recorded (ADR/ADL) where the slice changes a cycle rule
- [ ] `quality-gate` green, changeset, reviewed (risk:red: explicit human approval); PR says `Part of #641`

## Story Sizing and Sprint Readiness

**Final Story Points**: L (5)
**Confidence Level**: Medium
**Sizing Justification**: 2 tasks, about 18 h, carried from #641 with their estimates.
**Sprint Fit Assessment**: sized to fit one implement stage (the whole #641, 118 h, ended `incomplete` three times).

## Dependencies and Coordination

> **Blocked by #652 (refinement first).** Do not implement until #652 is refined and this card is re-analysed against it: maxRounds, group size and groups per round become parameters of a loop block. Status moved back to Todo on 2026-11-14. Order: #652 refinement → #617 → re-analysis of #648, #649, #650.

**Prerequisite**: #646 (catalogue for the round-3 escalation), #648 (preflight before parallel prepare).
**Dependent**: #650.

## Validation and Testing Strategy

**Testing Methods**: the test plan above, at the levels stated; `quality-gate`.
**Success Metrics**: contributes to the #641 targets (AC-19, measured in #650).

## Assumptions

- **Parallelism scope?** Prepare and validate in parallel; greens serial. Evidence: the contract loop is 36% of time, and greens write the same PR branch. Overturn: parallel greens on disjoint paths.
- **Custody tests?** AC-4 (#648) is re-run here; this story removes no HALT or custody rule. Overturn: none.
- **One stage?** This slice is self-contained and deliverable in one implement stage. Evidence: maintainer split decision 2026-11-14 after three `incomplete` attempts on #641. Overturn: split further.

## Notes and Additional Context

Split from #641 on 2026-11-14 (maintainer decision). Evidence, baseline and data points stay on #641 (Diagnosis and comments).

**Constraint (all child stories of #641)**: no custody, HALT or contract rule is removed; existing custody and contract tests stay green (pinned by AC-4 in #648); no secrets or card text in records; minimal code.

<details>
<summary>Proposals this slice implements (from #641)</summary>

| # | Change | Rule kept | Expected gain (from the data) | Risk / mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P4 | **Round discipline**: a re-review blocks only on the delta, prior findings, or a Critical or security finding (new out-of-delta findings become a follow-up card). Minor-only findings never open a round alone. After round 3, Minor-only goes to ready-for-merge with a follow-up, and a remaining Major escalates. | review independence, blocking Major/Critical | median rounds **3 → ≤ 2**, max **6 → 3**; about 60 min active saved per removed round | real defects deferred → Critical/security always blocks; follow-up card always filed |
| P5 | **Fewer, parallel groups**: at most 3 groups per round, merged by owner. Groups with disjoint fixScope and no `dependsOn` run prepare + validate in parallel worktrees. Greens stay serial, and one verify per round runs on the merged head. | per-group seal, `verify-chain` on the final head | a #642-shape round: 7 serial chains → 3 groups, 2 contract loops in parallel, about **−50% round wall** | worktree contention → disjoint fixScope required; custody verified on the merged head |

</details>

## Technical Analysis

### Implementation Approach

Design: not required.

Review-phase and `resolve` rules for out-of-delta findings, Minor-only and round 3. Red-spec planner cap of 3 groups; driver runs prepare/validate of disjoint groups in parallel worktrees, greens serial, one verify on the merged head.

### Technical Risks and Mitigation

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| real defects deferred | escaped defect | Critical/security always blocks; follow-up card always filed |
| parallel prepare collides on fixtures | flaky seals | disjoint fixScope check fails closed; separate worktrees |

## Task Breakdown

Task ids kept from #641.

- [ ] **T-8**: Round discipline
- [ ] **T-9**: Group cap and parallel prepare/validate

### Dependency Graph

```text
T-8, T-9 (independent; T-9 after #648)
```

### AC Coverage

| AC | Tasks |
| --- | --- |
| AC-14 | T-8 |
| AC-16 | T-9 |

### Tasks

**T-8** (Development, ~8h): review-phase and `resolve` rules: out-of-delta new findings become non-blocking follow-ups unless Critical or security; Minor-only opens no round; the round-3 rule.

**T-9** (Development, ~10h): red-spec planner cap of 3 groups. The driver runs prepare and validate of disjoint groups in parallel worktrees, greens serial, and one verify on the merged head.
title: Delivery cycle: round discipline and fewer, parallel fix groups (#641 slice 5/6)

The Viewer job used the *same* real SAF callback test and failed a `not displayed` assertion. These are distinct failure classes; logging did not prove which state blocked login.

**Narrow test-only [Draft PR #2798](https://github.com/lazyxu/xdrive/pull/2798), exact HEAD `8fe66f0f36a9bfaa40c661df88d2b2c6980e32e6`:**
- Keep original full `Screen.FILES && loaded` **10,000 ms** Compose wait; if it times out, report **fixture-only safe** screen/loading/loaded/itemCount/pathDepth/factoryCount. Do not log Server URL, account, input, JWT, filesystem path or full UI semantics.
- Open real account menu and `performScrollTo().assertIsDisplayed().assertIsEnabled().performClick()` for actual SAF upload action; preserve real callback count = exactly 1.
- No runtime Android code, mock substitute, skipped assertions or extra timeout. Must pass genuine API35 instrumentation on this exact SHA plus CI Final Gate. One passing attempt is evidence, **not** proof intermittent failure is resolved. If still RED, use the sanitized state to isolate Controller/fixture race before changing production.

This PR does not supersede the independent SDK image corruption diagnostic. Keep Issue open for stable repeated source-exact evidence and remediation, not blanket Android CI exemptions.

---

## Cross-PR real Android Compose instrumented CI RED (2026-10-24)

Three unrelated source-only PRs hit **different actual instrumentation assertions** on current Android Kotlin source:

- [#2027 CI #40084472996](https://github.com/lazyxu/xdrive/actions/runs/40084472996): `VisualParityTest.passwordRevealResetsAfterBlurAndEmpty` failed `assertExists` for `隐藏密码`. PR modified only Linux host migration scripts/docs, and later merged after independent CI evidence.
- [#2507 CI #40092649610](https://github.com/lazyxu/xdrive/actions/runs/40092649610/job/120868331007): `VisualParityTest.narrowLargeFontSubmitRemainsReachable` exceeded `compose.waitUntil(timeoutMillis=10_000)` in `loginScreen`. Exact HEAD only changes Go/Chromium/U01 test fixtures; source-level real Go/PG17 original U01 and 8-cycle ABBA passed on same head. Failed Android job is independently being rerun rather than skipped.
- [#2539 CI #40093208827](https://github.com/lazyxu/xdrive/actions/runs/40093208827/job/120870412958): `DriveAppTest.loginBrowseDetailsBackAndLogout` exceeded 10s `ComposeUiTest.waitUntil` in `startAndLogin`. PR only adds Caddy operator bootstrap files.

Common source: `android/app/src/androidTest/java/com/tfluid/xdrive/VisualParityTest.kt`, `DriveAppTest.kt`, synthetic `DriveController(scope, { fixtureService })` whose Main dispatcher/StateFlow operations are not necessarily completed by Compose idle. #2512 and #2522 already added bounded readiness waits and **must not** be reverted or counted as fully resolving all tests.

### Scoped next work

1. Compare actual Android failure XML/Compose UI hierarchy and controller `Screen.CONNECT/LOGIN/FILES`, `loaded`, dispatcher state at failure (only synthetic non-secret fixtures); distinguish a true product/fixture state defect, hidden keyboard/scroll click, lost callback, or emulator scheduling stall. The current log does not prove a unique root cause.
2. Test first with exact emulator API 35 and existing whole `:app:connectedDebugAndroidTest` 14-test gate under CI conditions. Record reproducibility across repeated **unchanged SHA** runs and do not claim two green retries establish a fix.
3. Fix deterministic fixture scheduling and/or real UI semantics without weakening assertions, skipping tests, replacing real Compose UI, mocking the product controller, or merely increasing timeout as a substitute for root cause.
4. Keep exact-HEAD Go/Web/Desktop/Windows/Android + Final Gate for dependent PRs; perform code-level authorization/Owner/route regressions normally. Do not use Android flake to suppress genuine U01 browser RED.

Production-only inaccessible security acceptance: **按用户决定跳过（未验收）**; controlled source and CI safety gates still mandatory.

### 2026-10-24: Viewer #2554 Android glyph test failure and scoped stabilization

- Exact `#2554@84a6d07b` [Android job](https://github.com/lazyxu/xdrive/actions/runs/40097694432/job/120883289823): **1/14** `VisualParityTest.brandAndFileTypeGlyphsRender` failed: expected 2 `文件夹` nodes, found zero immediately after synthetic login; Android APK, unit tests and lint all passed. Viewer PR changed zero Android files.
- `VisualParityTest.login()` clicked the actual Compose submit control and returned without waiting for the `DriveController` Main-coroutine `FILES/loaded` state. This is a plausible timing race, not proof of a root cause from the single failure; a first attempt rerun on unchanged SHA is still running.
- Opened test-only [PR #2559](https://github.com/lazyxu/xdrive/pull/2559) to wait at most **10s** for `PASSWORD&&!loading` or `FILES&&loaded&&!loading` before reading the same Compose UI. No assertion suppression, runtime/UI changes, or CI relaxation. Independently require accurate-head Android Native + full Final Gate.

- **Additional unchanged-HEAD attempt 2:** [#2554 CI #40097694432 / Android job #120888771929](https://github.com/lazyxu/xdrive/actions/runs/40097694432/job/120888771929) failed a **different** 1/14 Compose test: `VisualParityTest.narrowLargeFontSubmitRemainsReachable` timed out waiting 10 seconds for CONNECT→LOGIN. The previous attempt failed only the post-login glyph count. This cross-attempt alternation confirms the initial Viewer code change is not a reliable explanation; detailed synthetic fixture controller/Compose state diagnostics are still needed. PR #2559 covers the post-login missing wait only, **not** this distinct CONNECT failure.

- **PR #2559 exact-head Android green**: [CI #40099953883](https://github.com/lazyxu/xdrive/actions/runs/40099953883), test-only `3a517f54`: the unchanged genuine API-35 Android Native emulator gate passed all 14 tests after the bounded FILES/PASSWORD readiness wait. This is **one** passing run, not proof every CONNECT/narrow flake is eliminated. Full Final Gate and merge are still pending; no native test was skipped or relaxed.
title: CI(android): 定位真实 Compose 登录/SAF 偶发失败（诊断 PR #2798）

body:
> [!NOTE]
> GPT-6.1 Sol on behalf of PsychedelicShayna

## Product finding: cold highlighting stops early and does not automatically recover

The previously proposed test-only patch is **withdrawn and not ready to apply**. Removing cold-versus-warm equality would accept an incomplete terminal result. Content preservation and one non-null color do not establish correct syntax highlighting.

**(a) No automatic recovery exists in the inspected production consumers.** Sources below are pinned to nightly `05cc9be51403fcfa99b6f2de8dab28e6bc2dc4fb`, not inferred from a passing warm call:

- [Source highlight atom, lines 29–50](https://github.com/PsychedelicShayna/neocode/blob/05cc9be51403fcfa99b6f2de8dab28e6bc2dc4fb/apps/mobile/src/features/files/sourceHighlightingState.ts#L29-L50): the cache key is path/contents/theme. Any fulfilled `highlightSourceFile` result is success; only rejected Promises become errors. There is no completion-quality flag, retry, or highlighter-warmed dependency. Its five-minute **idle** TTL is cache retention, not periodic re-tokenization of a mounted view.
- [Source-file renderer, lines 128–148](https://github.com/PsychedelicShayna/neocode/blob/05cc9be51403fcfa99b6f2de8dab28e6bc2dc4fb/apps/mobile/src/features/files/SourceFileSurface.tsx#L128-L148): unchanged contents/path/theme keep the same atom; every successful result becomes `status = "ready"`. Warming the engine elsewhere does not invalidate that atom. [Rendering, lines 87–118](https://github.com/PsychedelicShayna/neocode/blob/05cc9be51403fcfa99b6f2de8dab28e6bc2dc4fb/apps/mobile/src/features/files/SourceFileSurface.tsx#L87-L118) uses returned token colors directly, so a single colored token paints the whole line uniformly; it is not evidence of complete classification.
- [File preload, lines 57–74](https://github.com/PsychedelicShayna/neocode/blob/05cc9be51403fcfa99b6f2de8dab28e6bc2dc4fb/apps/mobile/src/features/files/preload-workspace-file.ts#L57-L74): it primes the **same** source-highlight atom. It can cache the incomplete result before the view opens; it does not perform a second complete pass.
- [Markdown highlight atom/hook, lines 38–87](https://github.com/PsychedelicShayna/neocode/blob/05cc9be51403fcfa99b6f2de8dab28e6bc2dc4fb/apps/mobile/src/features/threads/markdownCodeHighlightState.ts#L38-L87): similarly caches a fulfilled snippet as success with no quality signal or automatic warm retry.
- [Native Markdown hook, lines 44–148](https://github.com/PsychedelicShayna/neocode/blob/05cc9be51403fcfa99b6f2de8dab28e6bc2dc4fb/apps/mobile/modules/t3-markdown-text/src/useHighlightedCode.ts#L44-L148): caches every resolved token array, commits it to React state, and then reuses that cache. It **does re-render when the Promise resolves**, but that render displays the same incomplete tokens; it does not re-tokenize them. Changing inputs or eventual cache eviction may happen to cause another call, but is not automatic recovery for unchanged visible content.
- [Incremental snippets, lines 19–65](https://github.com/PsychedelicShayna/neocode/blob/05cc9be51403fcfa99b6f2de8dab28e6bc2dc4fb/apps/mobile/src/features/review/incrementalSnippet.ts#L19-L65): completed-prefix tokens and the returned grammar state are retained without checking whether a line stopped early. Later appends can recompute the tail but retain an already incomplete completed line and its state. Appending is not a recovery mechanism for a stationary block.

[PROVEN source defect] Once TextMate returns `stoppedEarly`, Shiki discards that signal and the app can cache/display the incomplete classification as a finished result indefinitely while the input remains mounted and unchanged. Initializer completion is already awaited; another await on that same readiness Promise cannot repair the lost classification. This is a **production recovery defect**, not an invalid test contract. The controlled execution below demonstrates the real tokenizer's incomplete result; this consumer inspection establishes why it is not automatically repaired. No actual device screen was inspected.

**(b) A real-device line/file trigger threshold has not been measured.** The source establishes a per-line wall-clock condition, not a character-count or CPU-time threshold: `Date.now() - startTime > 500` between tokenizer scans. A synchronous regex scan is not preempted at 500 ms, so this is not a hard latency cap. Language/pattern complexity, first-use compilation, engine, CPU and scheduling determine whether it is crossed.

- [Application bounds, lines 52–54 and 504–552](https://github.com/PsychedelicShayna/neocode/blob/05cc9be51403fcfa99b6f2de8dab28e6bc2dc4fb/apps/mobile/src/features/review/shikiReviewHighlighter.ts#L504-L552): lines **over 1,000 characters** intentionally use plain tokens. Lines of 1,000 characters or less still enter tokenization and can hit the elapsed budget. Batches hold up to 200 short lines; the larger-file yield condition is over eight lines and only runs between batches/long-line boundaries. Neither batching nor file preloading detects or retries a stopped line. The 100,000-character snippet-session cutoff selects the existing fallback path; it is not a TextMate deadline trigger.
- The cold test's input is just `const answer: number = 42;` (**25 characters, one line**). The earlier discriminator forced a 501 ms elapsed-clock crossing; **it did not show that a natural 25-character line costs 500 ms on a device or a CI CPU**. The 771/831 ms CI case durations include setup and do not identify per-line time or stoppedEarly.
- [Engine choice, lines 46–51 and 222–311](https://github.com/PsychedelicShayna/neocode/blob/05cc9be51403fcfa99b6f2de8dab28e6bc2dc4fb/apps/mobile/src/features/review/shikiReviewHighlighter.ts#L222-L311): tests default to JavaScript regex; a normal React Native app prefers the native engine and can fall back to JavaScript. The installed native engine calls synchronous JSI scanner creation/search (`react-native-shiki-engine/src/engine/index.ts:16–39`), and C++ synchronously compiles/searches patterns (`cpp/onig_regex.cpp:100–150,158–217`). Its README supplies reuse/cache advice but no measured line-length/device timing threshold. JavaScript-worker timing is not a native-device measurement.

Outstanding empirical evidence, not a claimed finding: a cold real-device profile must record device/CPU, build/engine, language, input bytes/line lengths/count, initializer versus per-line elapsed time, and actual `stoppedEarly` before reporting a size threshold or incidence. No GUI/device launch or new test was performed for this source-only follow-up.

## Observed behavior and exact evidence boundary

The named mobile case is `apps/mobile/src/features/review/shikiReviewHighlighter.test.ts > initializes source and snippet highlighting without a warmup`.

- PR #30 [CI 38483661684](https://github.com/PsychedelicShayna/neocode/actions/runs/38483661684), source `5bac46aa18a3736050457b8300e19bda74fe5851`, Test job 115592023364: seven tests / one failure, cold-init case **771 ms**, other six pass. Later PR #30 [CI 38484379865](https://github.com/PsychedelicShayna/neocode/actions/runs/38484379865) passes all seven, while unrelated documented failures keep the global job red.
- Reported nightly baseline `d33113d39b16bb2cfa73c7aafd808d6385a4f9a0`, [CI 38487963157](https://github.com/PsychedelicShayna/neocode/actions/runs/38487963157): this file's seven tests pass; the cold case reports 496 ms. This is not an overall Test-job pass.
- PR #39 source `a85b2902d59172eb93c39e1f0cf4a87a4d12fb8a`, [CI 38488719620](https://github.com/PsychedelicShayna/neocode/actions/runs/38488719620), Test job 115608563313: seven tests / one failure, this case **831 ms**, other six pass.
- The unchanged cold case also passes at 422 ms in existing docs-head [CI 38492649021](https://github.com/PsychedelicShayna/neocode/actions/runs/38492649021).

[PROVEN observation limit] Full original Test-job logs, check-run annotations and artifact inventories were inspected, not just progress snippets. Neither failing run exposes the Shiki assertion/rejection: final failure inventories and annotations report only the separate desktop fixture or client-runtime timeout; each run's only artifact is `thread-transfer-results`, not a mobile error/JUnit report. Thus **which original assertion failed remains unknown**. A 771/831 ms progress duration is not evidence of a 5000 ms test timeout.

Accepted focused receipts remain [`PR #30 comment 6157374329`](https://github.com/PsychedelicShayna/neocode/pull/30#issuecomment-6157374329): exact cold-case CLI execution on base `934def55c9856d6d9791733aaddbbcda168521ce` passed one / skipped six in 1.17 s; head `25892368df471a35cde44888e5a9fdddeaedfcf9` passed one / skipped six in 1.16 s. Those tests were not repeated. Titania's complete `/tmp/titania-39-shiki-classification.md` confirms identical test/highlighter blobs across those SHAs, d331 and a85: `cfb28051cb1225767744cc89008186df481c8b28` / `9b69c8d552ea2dad0345586df7aec616f27d9195`. Live nightly GET also matches both investigated blobs.

## What cold initialization loads and awaits

[PROVEN source path]

- [`shikiReviewHighlighter.ts:1–11,46–73,233–249,277–281`](https://github.com/PsychedelicShayna/neocode/blob/a85b2902d59172eb93c39e1f0cf4a87a4d12fb8a/apps/mobile/src/features/review/shikiReviewHighlighter.ts#L1-L281): static imports bring in **seven grammar modules**—bash, JavaScript, JSON, JSX, TSX, TypeScript, YAML—and **two themes**, `github-light-default` / `github-dark-default`. Core initialization registers the initial/embedded grammar graph and both themes, not only the requested TypeScript/dark pair. Other supported languages use later dynamic imports, not this cold case.
- At `:46–51`, test mode defaults to **JavaScript regex**, unless `EXPO_PUBLIC_REVIEW_HIGHLIGHTER_ENGINE` overrides it. The default path creates `createJavaScriptRegexEngine()` and does **not** fetch/instantiate Oniguruma WASM. Explicit native preference probes `react-native-shiki-engine`; unavailable/failed native initialization falls back to JavaScript. The original runs' complete effective engine environment is not captured by their Shiki failure detail; do not claim their preference was independently measured.
- Installed `apps/mobile/node_modules/@shikijs/core/dist/index.mjs:1043–1055` and `node_modules/.pnpm/@shikijs+primitive@4.2.0/node_modules/@shikijs/primitive/dist/index.mjs:202–206,236–243,305–317,481–493`: the constructor awaits engine/language/theme resolution, then builds its registry, normalizes themes and registers grammars. Here those inputs are already imported objects, not network fetches. Missing required embedded grammar can throw. **Initialization completion does not precompile every regex used on the first line.**
- Installed JavaScript engine `apps/mobile/node_modules/@shikijs/engine-javascript/dist/engine-compile.mjs:7–20,30–43` and `scanner-DX8LRFGE.mjs:7–29,51–67`: Oniguruma patterns are translated into JavaScript RegExp; an engine-local cache retains compiled patterns/errors; the initial regex work and execution are synchronous CPU work. Fake timers or a sleep cannot make that compilation finish sooner.

[`getHighlighter():222–311`](https://github.com/PsychedelicShayna/neocode/blob/a85b2902d59172eb93c39e1f0cf4a87a4d12fb8a/apps/mobile/src/features/review/shikiReviewHighlighter.ts#L222-L311) assigns one module-scoped construction Promise before yielding control. Concurrent callers share it; success stays cached, rejection resets it to null. `highlightLines():504–527` awaits this Promise before tokenization. `loadSingleLanguage():340–373` joins an existing per-language Promise, awaits the importer **and** `highlighter.loadLanguage`, then records admission and deletes the in-flight entry. The cold test uses preloaded TypeScript/`ts`, so it never enters that dynamic-language path.

## The second deadline: real 500 ms per-line tokenization

[PROVEN mechanism, independent of Vitest's test timeout]

Installed Shiki primitive `.../@shikijs+primitive@4.2.0/.../dist/index.mjs:618–620,654–668,702–708` defaults `tokenizeTimeLimit = 500` and passes it to `grammar.tokenizeLine2`. The application passes no override. Installed TextMate `.../@shikijs+vscode-textmate@10.0.2/.../dist/index.js:1812–1822,2438–2443,3007–3016` checks **`Date.now() - startTime > timeLimit`** and returns a normal result with **`stoppedEarly: true`**, not a rejected Promise.

Shiki consumes the returned tokens/state but does not inspect `stoppedEarly`; its last token covers the remaining input. Consequently the text can be intact and non-null colors present while token boundaries/colors are incomplete. A first cold regex scan or descheduling can consume this wall-clock budget; a warmed second call can finish normally.

The test [`:50–71`](https://github.com/PsychedelicShayna/neocode/blob/a85b2902d59172eb93c39e1f0cf4a87a4d12fb8a/apps/mobile/src/features/review/shikiReviewHighlighter.test.ts#L50-L71) first awaits cold source highlighting, verifies text/colors, then awaits a warm snippet call and at line 70 requires **exact token-array equality**. A cutoff can make that comparison fail even though initialization finished. Because the consumer treats the returned result as final and has no automatic recovery, the mismatch exposes lost syntax classification; it is not grounds to weaken the assertion.

## Shared state, resets and concurrency

[PROVEN source; no demonstrated readiness race]

- Per application-module generation: `highlighterPromise`, `loadedLanguages`, `languageLoadingPromises`, normalized-line and snippet-session WeakMaps (`shikiReviewHighlighter.ts:64–74,178,412–427,559–612`). Core also owns mutable theme/grammar registry and an engine-local regex cache/lastIndex. Tokenization/registration mutate synchronously on one JS worker; regex lastIndex is reset before execution.
- The file has no `.concurrent`, test-local fake timers, hooks or mocks. Vitest's default `sequence.concurrent` is false; its runner awaits sequential children (`@vitest/runner/dist/chunk-artifact.js:1771–1772,3146–3160`). The source call and snippet call are serial and both awaited. Worker files/packages may compete for CPU, not share these module variables under default isolation.
- `vi.resetModules()` in the cold case invalidates evaluated module entries but does not rewrite original top-level import bindings or call `highlighter.dispose` (`vitest/dist/chunks/utils.BX5Fg8C4.js:29–42`). The original warmed highlighter and a new cold application-module singleton can coexist; later tests retain the original imports. Externalized dependency caches can survive reset, so this is not a completely new process.
- Shiki has a disposal API (`primitive/dist/index.mjs:376–389,451–469`); this application module never calls it. Resource retention across these two module generations is a source fact, **not proof it caused the failure**. No overlapping initializer/admission mutation is demonstrated for this preloaded one-line case.
- Chunking yields through `setTimeout(0)` only for larger batches (`shikiReviewHighlighter.ts:52–54,531–552`); these one-/three-/four-line test inputs do not take that path. Snippet-session caching is irrelevant because the tests supply no session.
- CI runs up to four non-server package tasks concurrently (`ci.yml:71–75,113`). The original effective mobile configuration is not captured; neither the package/default-versus-root test timeout nor a hook timeout explains the observed subsecond failure without an actual timeout error.

## Cause hypotheses, ranked by evidence

1. **[PROVEN feasible mechanism; INFERENCE attribution to original CI] Internal 500 ms budget stops the cold first tokenization, warm tokenization completes, and line 70's cold-versus-warm equality detects incomplete cold classification.** Source shows the silent partial result and cache-dependent work. The single private discriminator below reproduces precisely that outcome while all readiness/content/color checks pass. Original failing assertion and actual `stoppedEarly` were not recorded, so this is not claimed as the confirmed historical cause.
2. **[INFERENCE, weaker] Initialization/regex/grammar rejection or explicit native-engine override interacts with reset/external dependency caching.** These error paths exist and reset the Promise, but original rejection details are missing. A deterministic unsupported TypeScript pattern is less consistent with six neighboring passes and later unchanged all-file passes. No import-admission race is demonstrated.
3. **[PROVEN retained instances; INFERENCE impact] Reset leaves old/new highlighter generations undisposed, potentially adding memory/GC pressure.** There are only two visible generations in this file; no resource profile proves a causal slowdown.
4. **[NO supporting evidence] Missing completion await, shared Promise race between concurrent tests, WASM cold boot, or a 5 s/hook timeout.** Readiness and language admission are already awaited, tests are sequential, the default test engine is JavaScript, and the available progress rows are below 1 s.

## One discriminating private execution

The **one authorized private focused command** ran two diagnostic files/cases: this discriminator and #41's bounded fixture. Both passed; total 4.06 s; this discriminator's Vitest case was 981 ms. It used the **real production module, Shiki core, themes, grammar and JavaScript engine**. A transparent factory wrapper recorded the real grammar's `stoppedEarly` and budget. Only the first synchronous tokenizer call in the stressed case advanced `Date.now` by 501 ms after an actual scan; the original function was restored in `finally`, before returning to the test runner. No real sleep, global fake timers, production edit or timeout change.

- Normal control: source and snippet both `budget=500`, `stoppedEarly=false`, 11 tokens each, equal arrays.
- Controlled budget crossing: source `stoppedEarly=true` / one token; warm snippet `stoppedEarly=false` / 11 tokens; **unequal arrays**. Both returned the exact input text and non-null colors; initialization resolved successfully.

[PROVEN] The current line-70 requirement can fail solely because the production budget cuts syntax classification short, not because initialization was unawaited. That does not make partial classification acceptable: production currently has no completion signal or automatic recovery. [INFERENCE] The same mechanism caused the recorded CI flake. This was a controlled elapsed-clock discriminator, **not** a natural reproduction of the missing original assertion or a repeated old smoke test.

## Executable production specification

**Recommendation: (a), with (b)'s cache invariant, implemented below the consumers.** Observe the raw cutoff, keep the existing request pending, and perform one scheduled warm retry with a larger bounded budget. Do not resolve/cache the partial array as success. The public async functions continue returning token arrays, but fulfillment now means either complete tokenization or the existing intentional plain fallback; callers do not need a new partial-success schema. This is a production change, not the withdrawn assertion-removal patch.

### Exact loss point and affected call sites

[PROVEN installed source, Shiki 4.2.0 / TextMate 10.0.2]

- `node_modules/.pnpm/@shikijs+primitive@4.2.0/node_modules/@shikijs/primitive/dist/index.mjs:620`: default `tokenizeTimeLimit = 500`.
- **`:654` calls `grammar.tokenizeLine2(line, stateStack, tokenizeTimeLimit)`; `:655–668` consumes only tokens; `:702–708` saves `result.ruleStack` and returns tokens/state without `result.stoppedEarly`. This is the information-loss boundary.** `:612–616` then attaches that state to the returned array, making an interrupted state available through `getLastGrammarState`.
- TextMate `node_modules/.pnpm/@shikijs+vscode-textmate@10.0.2/node_modules/@shikijs/vscode-textmate/dist/index.js:1812–1821,2438–2444` returns a normal result with `stoppedEarly = true` when elapsed wall time exceeds the per-line limit. It does not throw.
- [Source/review batch call: `shikiReviewHighlighter.ts:523–527`](https://github.com/PsychedelicShayna/neocode/blob/1e1975dbc8ea495759a10d90940880f1faa80784/apps/mobile/src/features/review/shikiReviewHighlighter.ts#L518-L527) loses the flag before normalization. [Completed-prefix call: `incrementalSnippet.ts:29–39`](https://github.com/PsychedelicShayna/neocode/blob/1e1975dbc8ea495759a10d90940880f1faa80784/apps/mobile/src/features/review/incrementalSnippet.ts#L26-L39) then consumes the incomplete last state; [tail call: `:43–46`](https://github.com/PsychedelicShayna/neocode/blob/1e1975dbc8ea495759a10d90940880f1faa80784/apps/mobile/src/features/review/incrementalSnippet.ts#L41-L46) has the same loss.
- [Source entry: `shikiReviewHighlighter.ts:615–621`](https://github.com/PsychedelicShayna/neocode/blob/1e1975dbc8ea495759a10d90940880f1faa80784/apps/mobile/src/features/review/shikiReviewHighlighter.ts#L615-L621), snippet entry/read `:564–612`, and [selected review lines: `:647–649`](https://github.com/PsychedelicShayna/neocode/blob/1e1975dbc8ea495759a10d90940880f1faa80784/apps/mobile/src/features/review/shikiReviewHighlighter.ts#L647-L650) must all pass through the recovery boundary. Selected addition/deletion calls can overlap asynchronously; one request must not consume another request's cutoff/state.

[PROVEN available seam] The installed `@shikijs/types@4.2.0/dist/index.d.mts:775,830,843–845,407–418` exposes `getLanguage`, `codeToTokensBase`, `getLastGrammarState`, `tokenizeTimeLimit` and `grammarState`. Primitive `index.mjs:394–399,594–600` shows that registered grammar is the same object used for tokenization. The earlier transparent discriminator observed real `tokenizeLine2` results at this seam; this does not establish performance of the new recovery design.

### Options and decision

| Option | Correctness / cost | Disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| (a) Propagate cutoff; idle re-tokenization with a larger budget | Gives a concrete recovery path, retaining the pre-attempt grammar checkpoint. Requires a cutoff fence before Shiki discards the flag and a deferred retry. | **Choose.** Keep 500 ms first-pass budget; one retry at 1,000 ms per line after an idle turn. These numbers are a design choice, not a measured device latency guarantee. |
| (b) Mark partial and avoid success caching; retry once warm | Required invariant. Publishing partial metadata to every consumer would expand types and duplicate retry/state machinery. | **Apply centrally:** withhold partial tokens and leave the existing Promise/atoms pending until retry completes. No partial array reaches a success cache. |
| (c) Warm grammars at highlighter init | Can shift first-use work, but a sample cannot cover every lazy/nested grammar pattern or prevent scheduling-induced cutoff. Adds startup work without proving completion. | **Not the fix.** No initialization-wide warm-up in this patch; consider only later if profiling justifies it, never as a substitute for cutoff detection. |

[DESIGN recommendation, not executed or benchmarked] A second complete pass should benefit from first-use scanner work already performed. That benefit is inferred; the correctness rule does not depend on it: a second cutoff must not be reported as a completed success.

### Implementation recipe and contracts

1. Add one app-owned, typed tokenizer boundary in `apps/mobile/src/features/review/` (for example a new `reviewTokenization.ts`), used by both `shikiReviewHighlighter.ts` and `incrementalSnippet.ts`. Keep Shiki's token/theme conversion and state association; do not copy its metadata decoder, edit `node_modules`, add a package, or raise the global test timeout.
2. For each loaded non-plain grammar, install a thin `tokenizeLine2` fence **once per actual grammar object** (a WeakSet avoids double wrapping, including aliases). Call the original method with its original receiver/arguments. If the raw result has `stoppedEarly`, throw a private typed cutoff signal **before Shiki can consume the partial tokens or stopped state**. Otherwise return the result unchanged. This is propagation as a control signal rather than a new public token-array format. Install lazily before tokenization so dynamically admitted languages receive the same fence. No shared mutable “last request stopped” flag across an await.
3. The async operation catches **only** that cutoff signal, discards the interrupted attempt, and schedules exactly one retry at `tokenizeTimeLimit: 1_000`. Preserve code/language/theme and the original **complete pre-attempt `grammarState`**; for the current 200-line API, replay only the affected batch from its complete batch-entry checkpoint, not from the interrupted result's `ruleStack` and not from the start of the whole file. Normal initialization/grammar errors are not reclassified or retried. First attempt stays explicitly 500 ms.
4. Reuse/extract the idle scheduling policy already at [ `useReviewDiffPrewarming.ts:19–36`](https://github.com/PsychedelicShayna/neocode/blob/1e1975dbc8ea495759a10d90940880f1faa80784/apps/mobile/src/features/review/useReviewDiffPrewarming.ts#L19-L36): `requestIdleCallback` with 2,000 ms scheduling timeout, 100 ms timer fallback when unavailable. Keep the extraction limited to scheduling, not unrelated prewarming. Allow an injected scheduler in the tokenizer factory for deterministic tests. Idle execution is still synchronous JS work, not a worker or a hard 1,000 ms latency cap.
5. If the warm retry also stops, reject with a typed incomplete-highlighting error through the existing failure path. Never resolve with the partial array, cache it as complete, disable the deadline, or enter an unbounded idle/tight-loop retry. This deliberately bounds recovery; **eventual complete highlighting is required for the deterministic cold-only cutoff case**, not falsely promised for a persistently non-completing tokenizer. Keep that limitation visible in the failure result.
6. Provide a synchronous complete-or-unavailable operation for `highlightCodeSnippet.read`: a cutoff returns `undefined` so the native Markdown hook takes its existing async path. It must not throw the private cutoff into React render or schedule jobs during render. The async path then owns recovery. Preserve the existing revision guard for overlapping incremental updates; a superseded request cannot commit a stale prefix/checkpoint.

### Consumer disposition

| Consumer | Required change / retained behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `shikiReviewHighlighter.ts:518–527,564–612,615–650` | Replace direct unguarded tokenization with the shared complete-or-recover adapter. Source files, ordinary snippets and selected review lines must all use it. Return types stay unchanged; normal normalization and word-diff projection stay unchanged. |
| `sourceHighlightingState.ts:29–50`, `SourceFileSurface.tsx:128–148` | Their producer must now fulfill **only** with complete/intentional-fallback tokens. Existing pending-to-success/ready logic is sufficient and should not gain a duplicate retry loop or partial-success branch. Exercise this real atom family in the cutoff regression; no gratuitous source-atom/renderer rewrite is needed. File preloads use that same repaired atom. |
| `markdownCodeHighlightState.ts:38–87` | Same complete-on-fulfillment invariant; retain existing atom cache/state shape and prove it remains pending during recovery rather than accepting a partial success. |
| `incrementalSnippet.ts:19–65` | **Must change:** async batch/tail calls use recovery; tokens and `getLastGrammarState` become cacheable only after a complete attempt. Preserve the last valid prefix on cutoff; synchronous reads return unavailable and defer to async recovery. A complete prefix may survive a stopped tail, but stopped prefix tokens/state must never be retained. |
| `apps/mobile/modules/t3-markdown-text/src/useHighlightedCode.ts:44–148` plus iOS/Android callbacks | Retain the cache/React commit only because their Promise/read inputs now satisfy the stronger contract. `read` must return undefined on cutoff; the Promise resolves after full recovery and triggers the existing re-render. No independent native-hook retry or callback/API change. Verify this consumer path as well as the atoms. |

### Acceptance tests and evidence requirements

These are implementation acceptance requirements, **not tests already run**. Use the existing focused mobile tests and atom/hook conventions; no real sleep, benchmark-sized fixture, flaky wall-clock race or unbounded wait.

1. **Deterministic cold slow-tokenizer seam:** inject a raw `tokenizeLine2` delegate/fence seam and a controllable idle scheduler. Exercise each consumer path independently with its own armed cutoff delegate and controllable scheduler. For a real TypeScript grammar/theme and `const answer: number = 42;`, make that path's first raw call return valid partial binary tokens with `stoppedEarly: true`; subsequent calls delegate to the real complete tokenizer. Do not expect multiple concurrent requests all to stop after one global once-only injection. This simulates the deadline outcome without sleeping or pretending a fake duration is a device measurement. Before draining the scheduled callback, the unchanged source and Markdown requests must not become success/ready or cache that partial line. After draining, their actual production results and the native Markdown hook's committed value must equal a real warmed **complete** reference for the same engine/language/theme and preserve exact text. Assert the eventual result/re-render, not just a non-null color, a call count or copied arguments. Keep the original cold/warm equality when the Promise now resolves complete.
2. **Prefix/state recovery:** cut off inside a completed multiline/comment/template prefix, then recover and append. Both the repaired prefix and subsequent lines must match complete full highlighting; a stopped `ruleStack` must not poison the cache. Retain the existing overlapping-update regression to prevent stale recovery overwriting a newer revision.
3. **Persistent cutoff:** force both attempts to stop. The existing consumer failure path receives an incomplete-highlighting error, with no partial success/cache and no endless retries. This tests the bounded failure contract rather than claiming guaranteed completion for arbitrary pathological regex work.
4. **Long-line fallback:** preserve the existing over-1,000-character plain-token regression and add the boundary only where needed: exactly 1,000 remains eligible for syntax tokenization; 1,001 yields the exact original text with null color/fontStyle, does not enter the grammar/recovery seam, and does not suppress highlighting of an adjacent eligible line. That plain fallback remains a valid completed result, not a retry/error. Preserve unsupported-language fallback as well.
5. Run the affected focused mobile tests after implementation and require the issue's hosted CI coverage. The source inspection and earlier controlled probe are not a passing implementation receipt. Keep real-device timing/engine/incidence as unmeasured until separately profiled; native mobile GUI proof remains with the authorized owner, not this specification brief.

The old test-only patch remains withdrawn. This specification is executable for its own baseline production issue; it does not claim a production patch exists or that the missing historical CI assertion has been recovered. Priority stays p2: an exposure/recovery defect is proven in source, but widespread natural native-device incidence has not been measured. Effort is medium because the fence, bounded recovery, synchronous read and prefix state must work across all consumers. Scheduling after Titania's current queue is **Europa/Jupiter's decision**; this brief creates no queue entry, ordering edge or implementation assignment.

## Scope

Current authorization is an executable production specification plus existing-label triage only. No repository source edit, implementation branch/worktree, install, GUI/device launch, CI rerun or new test execution. The earlier one private two-case discriminator was not repeated. No queue/blocker/dependency changes; Europa/Jupiter own placement after the current implementation queue.
title: fix(mobile): cold highlighting stops early without recovery
